hook: The composer of the Ring, who built his own opera house, and whose music still divides people.

pages.x: Richard Wagner was born in Leipzig in 1813, and grew up around the theatre, as his stepfather was an actor. As a teenager he heard Beethoven and decided to become a composer, mostly teaching himself.
In 1839, deep in debt, he slipped across the border from Riga at night and fled by ship to London. A terrible storm at sea gave him the idea for his opera The Flying Dutchman, about a ghost ship.
As conductor of the opera in Dresden he joined the revolution of 1849. When it failed, there was a warrant for his arrest, and he fled to Switzerland, where he lived in exile for more than ten years.
In his opera Lohengrin, first staged in 1850, a chorus leads the bride and groom to their room. Today the Bridal Chorus is played at weddings all over the world.

In 1864, broke and on the run from people he owed money, he got a message: the new king of Bavaria, 18-year-old Ludwig II, adored his music. The king paid his debts and supported him for the rest of his life.

His greatest work, The Ring of the Nibelung, is four operas, about 15 hours of music, about gods, dwarfs, a magic ring and the end of the world. He worked on it for 26 years. In this famous music, warrior maidens ride through the sky.

He built his own opera house at Bayreuth, with the orchestra hidden in a covered pit and the hall dark during the show, both new ideas then. It opened in 1876 with the first full Ring, and the festival still runs every summer.

Wagner was vain and selfish, borrowed money he never repaid, and wrote a hateful essay attacking Jews. Long after he died in Venice in 1883, Hitler worshipped his music, and it is still rarely played in Israel.
Wagner changed opera into "music drama", joining music, poetry and stage, and his rich harmonies shaped the music that came after him, all the way to film scores.
pts: Wrote The Ring of the Nibelung
His music still shapes film scores
